title_native: ダークサモナーとデキている
pullquote: Roni's desperate attempts to pray away his guilty conscience turn this situationship into top-tier late-night comedy. If you thought they could keep their secret hidden from the party for one more week, think again.
quick_take: Roni's desperate attempts to pray away his guilty conscience turn this situationship into top-tier late-night comedy. If you thought they could keep their secret hidden from the party for one more week, think again.
one_sentence_verdict: A riotous, fast-paced comedy midpoint that proves hiding a fantasy situationship is ten times harder—and funnier—than slaying the demon king.
synopsis_paragraphs: The cold sweat hits before the door even swings open. We have hit the mid-season mark, and you can practically smell the panic burning through the screen. Roni and Amona are supposed to be sworn enemies—a sanctified priest bound by holy vows and a dark summoner drenched in demonic pacts. Instead, they are stuck in the most awkward walk-of-shame holding pattern in fantasy anime history, scrambling to adjust collars, hide summoned familiars, and pretend nothing happened when the rest of the party comes knocking.

What makes this episode click is how relentlessly it escalates the farce. It is not just the guilt; it is the sheer absurdity of Roni trying to maintain a pious moral high ground while Amona's smug façade completely collapses the moment anyone breathes in their direction. You do not get a second of breathing room. The pacing drops you straight into the frantic beats of hiding under covers and suffocating whispers, tapping right into the classic screwball energy that made early late-night ecchi hits so addictive.
sakuga_paragraphs:
- **The Deadpan Cut:** Director Seiya Miyajima treats silence like a physical weapon. Right after a frantic scramble to hide evidence, the camera snaps wide, the background track cuts to absolute zero, and we get three excruciating seconds of Roni staring unblinkingly at the wall. That beat of dead air lets the ridiculousness sink in before the punchline drops.
- **Snap Expressions and Chief AD Snappy Frames:** Takahiro Sasaki's character designs really bend to the comedy here. Watch the smear frames whenever Amona loses her cool; her expression snaps instantly from high-and-mighty dark summoner smugness to wide-eyed, blushing disaster within two frames. It keeps the energy punchy without needing bloated action animation.
- **Audio Whiplash:** Sound director Fumihiko Ootera leans hard on jarring contrasts. You will hear an orchestral, sanctified choir swell up like Roni is receiving divine revelation, only for it to be violently choked off by a cartoonish thud or a smothered squeak. It sells the internal meltdown better than any inner monologue could.
story_paragraphs:
- **「インプ有能すぎる」 (*inpu yuunou sugiru* / "The imp is way too competent"):** Late-night boards on 5ch and X explode with this every time the little troublemaker steps in. The Imp is practically the audience surrogate at this point, orchestrating chaos just to force these two stubborn idiots into the same room.
- **「実質純愛」 (*jisshitsu jun'ai* / "Basically pure love"):** Even with all the ecchi setups and demonic contracts, timelines immediately hit this tag. Fans love pointing out that despite the scandalous premise, Roni and Amona act more like flustered middle-school sweethearts than dark fantasy rivals.
voice_paragraphs: - Yuuki Nishiyama delivers an absolute masterclass in suppressed panic as Roni. His voice constantly teeters on the edge of cracking as he tries to keep his low, priest-like baritone steady while speaking at a frantic hundred miles an hour. Playing off him, Rei Takano nails Amona's switch between haughty demonic threats and tiny, muffled squeals of embarrassment, turning their back-and-forth into rapid-fire comedic perfection.
takeaway_paragraphs: A riotous, fast-paced comedy midpoint that proves hiding a fantasy situationship is ten times harder—and funnier—than slaying the demon king. You can catch the latest chaos streaming exclusively on HIDIVE.
